sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Pradeep Kumar Naveriya - Advocate for the appl  Smt Nalini Gurung - Panel Lawyer for the respondent  ORDER Heard.
2.
This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail.

3. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in relation to FIR bearing Crime No.65/2025 registered at Police Station - Khatiya, District Mandla (M.P.), for the offence punishable under Sections 318(4),
61(2) of B.N.S. 2023.
4.

As per the case diary, Crime No. 65/2025 has been registered at Police Station Khatiya, District Mandla (M.P.), for the offences punishable under Sections 318(4) and 61(2) of the BNS, 2023 (corresponding to Sections 420 and 120-B of the IPC), against the present applicant.

It is alleged therein that the applicant, along with one another Sanjay Thakur, had assured the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:120 2 MCRC-56852-2025 complainant that they would secure his appointment to the post of Police Constable.

Since the complainant did not receive any appointment order from the competent authority, he demanded for returning of the amount allegedly paid by him to the applicant, and on such basis, the present crime has been registered on the basis of cheating and criminal conspiracy.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant sanguinely submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the alleged crime.

He also submits that the complainant has paid certain amounts to the applicant during the month of September 2023 to November 2023 on demand of the applicant Junaid Gani Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184191366/
1 for meeting his agricultural equipment's.

sentences.text: Applicant did not repay the amount taken from the complainant for some reason.

Consequently, with an oblique motive to pressurize the applicant for recovery of the amount allegedly borrowed by the applicant, the complainant has lodged a false and concocted complaint before the police.

He further submitted that on the relevant point of time there was no advertisement or recruitment of Police Constable as also there is no evidence to show that the complainant has submitted application/form to the concerned Government Department at any point of time, which itself demonstrate the false implication of the applicant.

On these premise,
learned counsel prays that the applicant may be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

6. Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application and submits that there is documentary evidence of making payment of Rs.4,54,000/- by way of bank account and UPI and some other amount was paid in cash thus total amount of Rs.6,50,000/- has been given by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:120 3 MCRC-56852-2025 complainant to the applicant.
Therefore, he prays for outright dismissal of the application.

7. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and on perusing the case diary, this Court is of the view that, if any amount at all paid by the complainant for securing an appointment to the post of Police Constable, would itself constitute an unlawful act on the part of the complainant.
Moreover, there is no direct or cogent material on record to establish that the complainant paid a total sum of Rs.6,50,000/- to the applicant.
In such circumstance, the applicant is not required to be subjected to custodial interrogation for the purpose of investigation in the present matter.

8. Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and without commenting on the merits of the case, it is a fit case, in which applicant may be given protection from his arrest in the aforesaid crime.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer/Arresting Officer of the Police Station concerned.
9. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 482(2) of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
10. MCrC stands disposed of.

(RAMKUMAR CHOUBEY) JUDGE NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:120 4 MCRC-56852-2025 Vin**
